note: Golden briefs for the editorial-motion system. The prompts are the real work — the kind of thing that actually arrives — deliberately without design direction, because choosing the approach is what the skills are for. Extends the skill-creator evals.json schema with expected_load_order and must_not_load.
rubric: At 200px wide, is the finding still legible?
As a still screenshot, does it still work?
Could someone state the finding out loud after two seconds?

evals.name: stat-tile
evals.prompt: We've got a finding out of the latest Essential Report — 63% of Australians think the federal government isn't doing enough on cost of living. I need a single stat tile for Instagram, square. Can you put one together?
evals.expected_output: A square animated HTML tile carrying one number as the hero, on a paper ground, with one ambient and one accent move.
expectations: The finding, not the metric name, is the title
One ambient move and at most one accent move
The hero figure is not set in a serif or display face
A source line is present

evals.name: multi-panel-explainer
evals.prompt: I need an explainer for a client deck on how the stage 3 tax cuts changed between the original package and the revised one. Three or four panels, walking through it. The numbers are simple: original gave $9,075 a year to the top bracket and nothing under $45k; the revised version gives $4,529 to the top and $354 to someone on $40k.
evals.expected_output: A multi-panel animated explainer that sequences the comparison, one fact per panel, with persistent marks between panels rather than a fresh chart each time.
expectations: Panels sequence a single argument rather than repeating the same chart
No dual y-axes and no value printed on every data point
A source and sample-size line is present
Stagger sits in the 60-90ms band

evals.name: social-cut-9x16
evals.prompt: Need a 9:16 vertical for Instagram stories out of this: support for a four-day week is 71% among under-35s and 48% among over-55s. One finding, has to work with the sound off.
evals.expected_output: A 9:16 composition re-derived for vertical rather than a scaled 16:9 master, with platform safe areas respected and a first frame that works as a poster.
expectations: Type is re-derived for vertical, not scaled down from a wide master
The focal point sits clear of platform chrome
The first frame works as a still poster
The piece reads with no audio

evals.name: report-visual
evals.prompt: Doing a visual for the Essential Report quarterly — trust in institutions over time. Six institutions, 2019 through to 2026, all trending down except the ABC which is basically flat. It sits in a PDF report so it needs to work as a still.
evals.expected_output: A still-first multi-series chart that survives print, with the ABC's flatness as the finding rather than six equally weighted lines.
expectations: One series is weighted as the finding; the rest recede
No colour-per-category when the story is one contrast
Works with no motion at all
A source and sample-size line is present

evals.name: product-mockup
evals.prompt: We're pitching a client on a dashboard product next week. I want a hero visual for the front of the pitch deck — the app UI floating, something that feels expensive, a bit of camera movement.
evals.expected_output: A lit-object composition with depth of field and a camera-style move, in the premium register rather than the data-journalism one.
expectations: Depth of field and a light source that reads as physical
Camera-style movement rather than element-by-element entrance
The house timing kit still governs durations
The ban on decorative gradients is applied with the premium carve-out, not ignored

evals.name: single-number-chart
evals.prompt: The whole story here is one number: 1 in 3 renters have gone without heating to make rent. Make me a chart.
evals.expected_output: A stat tile rather than a chart — the correct answer is to refuse the chart form, because a one-bar bar chart is on the ban list.
expectations: The output is a stat tile, not a one-bar bar chart or a two-slice pie
The number is the hero and is legible at 200px
tabular-nums is not applied to the standalone figure
A source line is present
